column7: TransitionMachineIdentity's post-commit, best-effort auth-cache eviction (internal/core/machine_identities.go) had no recover() around its MachineTokenHashes lookup, so a PANIC there (not just a returned error) unwound past an ALREADY-COMMITTED suspend/revoke, was caught by the outer HTTP Recovery middleware, and misreported a successful revoke as a 500 -- oracle (a). Found by FuzzStorageFaultOperations (server/faultops), fault=ListMachineIdentityCredentials#1/panic, crashing input ff58003231, now a permanent seed at server/faultops/testdata/fuzz/FuzzStorageFaultOperations/0134bc8cffdd0cfe. Confirmed the panic reproduces identically on the pre-existing fresh-per-call fuzz path too (not introduced by the in-flight world-reuse perf PR #2296 that found it faster). Fix: evictMachineIdentityCacheOrFlush recovers the panic and, on either a panic or a persistent lookup error after one retry, fails CLOSED by flushing every machine-token entry in the HTTP auth cache (InvalidateAllMachineTokenCache, server/middleware/auth.go) rather than silently leaving the revoked identity's credentials live in cache -- broader than a precise per-hash evict, but bounded to machine principals only (human sessions/PATs untouched) and self-healing (every machine principal simply re-validates against the DB on its next request, which correctly reflects the now-committed state). The proving test red/green-verified: fails on both halves (500 response, AND the revoked token still authenticating) with the recover() reverted, passes with it restored.
